title: Analytical Validation of Telomere Analysis Technology for High-Throughput Analysis of Telomere Variables
author: de Pedro, Díez, et al.
materials: Cell lines frozen in liquid nitrogen were thawed (in RPMI1640 + 1% FBS [v/v]) and cell counts and cellular viability determined with an EVE™ Automated Cell Counter. Aliquots with viability lower than 60% were discarded. Cells were seeded in clear bottom, black-walled, 384-well plates at the density of 15,000 cells per well with 5 replicates of each sample and 8 replicates of each control cell line. After allowing attachment cells were fixed with methanol/acetic acid (3/1, vol/vol) and digestion with pepsin, the cells were washed several times in order to remove the components of seeding medium and serum that could cross-react with the probe in a non-specific way. Cell seeding, addition and removal of the reagents and washes are conducted using robots Freedom EVO2® and Fluent® by TECAN. Following the washings, the cells were hybridized in situ with a fluorescent Peptide Nucleic Acid (PNA) probe that recognizes three telomere repeats (Alexa488-OO-CCCTAACCCTAACCCTAA, Panagene Inc., South Korea). The PNA probe is a nucleotide analogue capable of binding to nucleic acids in a sequence-specific manner obeying the Watson-Crick base pairing rules. In PNA, the sugar phosphate backbone of nucleic acids has been replaced by a synthetic peptide backbone keeping the distances between bases exactly the same as in DNA or RNA; increasing affinity and stability. The hybridization step used a buffer that containing a blocking reagent that prevented non-specific binding (Roche Cat No. 11096176001), and extensive washes after the hybridization ensured removal of excess probe and weak, non-specific binding. After washing and 4′,6-diamidino-2-phenylindole (DAPI) staining, the wells were filled up with PBS and the plate stored at 4 °C until analyzed on the microscope.

TRL was used to compare quantitatively results derived from TAT. In brief, genomic DNA extracted from the cell lines was digested using a cocktail of frequent-cutting restriction enzymes that lack recognition sites in the telomeric and subtelomeric regions [39]. The intact telomeres (and some sub-telomeric DNA) from all chromosomes were then resolved by agarose gel electrophoresis, with the telomeric fragments being visualized by in-gel hybridization using the DIG-labelled telomere 18-mer probe (CCTAAA)3 (Sigma Aldrich). The varying lengths of telomeres were assessed by comparison to a DNA ladder comprised of known fragment sizes.

steps.title: Thaw cells and assess viability
steps.instruction: Thaw frozen cell lines in RPMI‑1640 medium containing 1 % (v/v) fetal bovine serum, count cells and determine viability using an EVE™ Automated Cell Counter; discard any aliquot with viability below 60 %.

substeps.instruction: Thaw cells in RPMI‑1640 + 1 % FBS (v/v).
Count cells and measure viability with EVE™ Automated Cell Counter.
Discard aliquots with viability < 60 %.

steps.title: Seed cells in 384‑well plates
steps.instruction: Using TECAN Freedom EVO2® and Fluent® robots, dispense 15 000 cells per well into clear‑bottom, black‑walled 384‑well plates, arranging five replicates for each sample and eight replicates for each control cell line.

substeps.instruction: Program Freedom EVO2®/Fluent® to add 15 000 cells per well.
Set up 5 replicates per sample and 8 replicates per control.

steps.title: Fix and permeabilize cells
steps.instruction: After cells have attached, fix them with methanol/acetic acid (3:1 v/v), then digest with pepsin, and perform several washes to remove residual medium and serum.

substeps.instruction: Fix cells with methanol/acetic acid (3 vol methanol : 1 vol acetic acid).
Digest fixed cells with pepsin.
Wash cells repeatedly to eliminate seeding medium and serum.

steps.title: Hybridize with telomere PNA probe
steps.instruction: Hybridize cells in situ with the Alexa488‑OO‑CCCTAACCCTAACCCTAA PNA probe (Panagene, South Korea) in a buffer containing Roche blocking reagent (Cat No. 11096176001); simultaneously hybridize control wells with the antisense PNA probe as a negative control.

substeps.instruction: Prepare hybridization buffer with Roche blocking reagent (Cat No. 11096176001).
Add Alexa488‑labeled telomere PNA probe to sample wells.
Add antisense PNA probe to designated control wells.

steps.title: Post‑hybridization washes and DAPI staining
steps.instruction: Carry out extensive washes to remove excess probe, stain nuclei with 4′,6‑diamidino‑2‑phenylindole (DAPI), fill each well with PBS, and store the plate at 4 °C until microscopy.

substeps.instruction: Perform multiple washes to eliminate unbound probe.
Stain cells with DAPI.
Add PBS to each well.
Store plate at 4 °C pending imaging.

steps.title: Acquire and process fluorescence images
steps.instruction: Capture images on the High Content Screening Opera System; analyze raw images with Acapella® software (Perkin Elmer), further process data with Life Length’s Plate Analyzer, unify and format results using Pentaho (Hitachi Vantara), and subtract background spot counts derived from antisense controls.

substeps.instruction: Image plates on Opera System.
Process images with Acapella®.
Analyze data with Plate Analyzer software.
Unify/format data with Pentaho.
Subtract background using antisense control spot counts.

steps.title: Perform bioinformatics and statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Use the KNIME platform together with R (v3.4.2) for clinical data modeling; generate visualizations with ggplot2 (v3.1.0).

steps.title: Conduct Terminal Restriction Fragment analysis
steps.instruction: Extract genomic DNA from the same cell lines, digest with a cocktail of frequent‑cutting restriction enzymes that lack telomeric/sub‑telomeric sites, separate fragments by agarose gel electrophoresis, visualize telomeric DNA by in‑gel hybridization with a DIG‑labelled telomere 18‑mer probe (CCTAAA)₃ (Sigma‑Aldrich), and determine telomere lengths by comparison to a DNA ladder of known fragment sizes.

substeps.instruction: Extract genomic DNA from cell lines.
Digest DNA with a cocktail of frequent‑cutting restriction enzymes (no telomeric sites).
Run digested DNA on agarose gel electrophoresis.
Hybridize gel in‑gel with DIG‑labelled telomere 18‑mer probe (CCTAAA)₃ (Sigma‑Aldrich).
Compare band positions to a DNA ladder to assess telomere length.
